data.definition: Equivalent in seriousness to; virtually the same as.
data.grammar_rule: Always use 'to' after 'tantamount'. Never use 'with'.
examples: Refusing to testify was seen as tantamount to an admission of guilt.
Her silence was tantamount to consent.
data.common_mistake: ❌ His action was tantamount with betrayal. ➜ ✅ His action was tantamount to betrayal.

data.definition: Feeling bored, frustrated, or impatient with something that has been happening for a long time.
data.grammar_rule: Use 'of' when 'tired' means fed up or annoyed. Use 'from' when physical exertion caused fatigue (tired from running).
examples: I am tired of waiting for the delayed bus.
She is tired of eating the same food every day.
data.common_mistake: ❌ He is tired from listening to complaints. ➜ ✅ He is tired of listening to complaints.

data.definition: Consistent with or faithful to a pledge, standard, or identity.
data.grammar_rule: Use 'true to' when adhering to promises or values.
examples: He stayed true to his word and paid back the loan.
Always remain true to yourself.
data.common_mistake: ❌ Stay true with your dreams. ➜ ✅ Stay true to your dreams.

data.definition: Having the distinctive qualities of a particular type of person or thing.
data.grammar_rule: Always use 'of' after 'typical'. Do NOT use 'for'.
examples: Such warm hospitality is typical of the local people.
It is typical of him to arrive late.
data.common_mistake: ❌ That mistake is typical for beginners. ➜ ✅ That mistake is typical of beginners.

data.definition: A compulsory contribution to state revenue.
data.grammar_rule: Always use 'tax ON' before taxed goods or income.
examples: The government introduced a higher tax on luxury imported cars.
A tax on sugary drinks aims to improve public health.
data.common_mistake: ❌ A tax for sugar. ➜ ✅ A tax on sugar.

data.definition: The possibility of trouble, danger, or ruin.
data.grammar_rule: Use 'threat OF' an impending bad outcome. Contrast with 'threat TO' a victim.
examples: The company operated under the constant threat of bankruptcy.
The threat of severe weather postponed the festival.
data.common_mistake: ❌ The threat for rain. ➜ ✅ The threat of rain.
data.related_forms: ⚡ Noun: 'the threat OF war' ➔ Noun contrast: 'a threat TO security'

data.definition: A person or thing likely to cause damage or danger.
data.grammar_rule: Use 'threat TO' when identifying the vulnerable target.
examples: Pollution poses a serious threat to marine ecosystems.
Cyber attacks are a growing threat to business continuity.
data.common_mistake: ❌ Climate change is a threat for wildlife. ➜ ✅ Climate change is a threat to wildlife.
data.related_forms: ⚡ Noun: 'threat TO security' ➔ Verb: 'threaten security' (no prep)

data.definition: A printed piece of paper giving the holder a right to enter a place or travel.
data.grammar_rule: Use 'ticket to' a place or event (ticket to Paris / ticket to the concert). 'Ticket for' is also used for events.
examples: I bought two tickets to the theater performance.
Where can I buy a ticket for the football match?
data.common_mistake: ❌ I need a ticket at Rome. ➜ ✅ I need a ticket to Rome.

data.definition: An appointed or suitable moment for something.
data.grammar_rule: Use 'time for' before nouns or gerunds (time for bed / time for lunch).
examples: It is time for lunch!
There is no time for hesitation now.
data.common_mistake: ❌ It is time to the meeting. ➜ ✅ It is time for the meeting.

data.definition: A journey or excursion to a place.
data.grammar_rule: Always use 'to' after 'trip' when specifying a travel destination.
examples: We are planning a weekend trip to Paris.
How was your recent trip to the mountains?
data.common_mistake: ❌ Our trip in Rome was wonderful. ➜ ✅ Our trip to Rome was wonderful.

data.definition: To lay hold of, receive, or transport.
examples: He takes medicine after meals.
She took a photo of the sunset.
They have taken many photos.

data.definition: To protect, mind, or handle responsibility for someone or something.
data.grammar_rule: Three-word inseparable phrasal idiom.
examples: She takes care of her elderly parents.
Don't worry about the bill; I will take care of it.
data.common_mistake: ❌ Take care for him. ➔ ✅ Take care of him.

data.pattern: take off (plane/success - VI) / take off [clothing] (VT separable)
data.definition: To leave the ground (aircraft), become successful, or remove clothing.
data.grammar_rule: Intransitive for planes/success ('The plane took off'). Separable transitive for clothing ('take off your coat' / 'take it off').
examples: The flight took off on schedule.
Please take off your shoes before entering.
It was hot, so he took it off.
data.common_mistake: ❌ Take off to your shoes. ➔ ✅ Take off your shoes.

data.definition: To speak to someone or converse about a subject.
data.grammar_rule: Intransitive verb taking 'to' or 'with' for the listener and 'about' for the topic.
examples: I need to talk to my manager about my schedule.
They talked about their favorite movies for hours.
data.common_mistake: ❌ We talked the problem. ➔ ✅ We talked about the problem.

data.definition: To converse or discuss a specific topic.
data.grammar_rule: Requires 'about' before the subject of discussion.
examples: We talked about our weekend plans over coffee.
What are you talking about?
data.common_mistake: ❌ We talked the movie. ➔ ✅ We talked about the movie.

data.definition: To address or speak to a person.
data.grammar_rule: Requires 'to' before the listener.
examples: She went to talk to the doctor.
Don't talk to strangers on the internet.
data.common_mistake: ❌ Talk at him politely. ➔ ✅ Talk to him politely.

data.definition: To interfere with something in an unauthorized or harmful way.
data.grammar_rule: Inseparable verb + preposition structure requiring 'with'.
examples: Someone tried to tamper with the security lock.
It is a crime to tamper with official evidence.
data.common_mistake: ❌ Tamper on the machinery. ➔ ✅ Tamper with the machinery.

data.definition: To impart knowledge or instruct.
examples: She teaches mathematics at university.
He taught us history last semester.
They have taught many students.

data.definition: To relate or communicate information.
examples: He tells interesting stories.
She told me the truth about the event.
They have told everyone the good news.

data.definition: To express gratitude to someone for a helpful action or gift.
data.grammar_rule: Direct transitive verb! Place the person immediately after 'thank', then use 'for' before the reason.
data.noun_parallel: ⚡ Verb: 'I thanked him for his help' ➔ Noun: 'My thanks FOR his help'
examples: We thanked our host for the wonderful dinner.
She thanked me for helping her move.
data.common_mistake: ❌ Thank to you for coming. ➔ ✅ Thank you for coming.

data.definition: To use the mind to consider.
examples: She thinks carefully before deciding.
He thought about the question for a while.
We have thought of a good plan.

data.definition: To consider or reflect deeply on something over a period of time.
data.grammar_rule: 'Think ABOUT' implies active mental consideration or deliberation.
examples: I need some time to think about your offer.
What are you thinking about so intently?
data.common_mistake: ❌ I am thinking of my future plans. ➔ ✅ I am thinking about my future plans.

data.definition: To produce an idea or hold an opinion about something.
data.grammar_rule: 'Think OF' is used for opinions ('What do you think of X?') or spontaneous ideas ('I thought of a plan').
examples: What do you think of his new proposal?
I can't think of her name right now.
data.common_mistake: ❌ What do you think about the movie? (when asking overall impression) ➔ ✅ What do you think of the movie?

data.definition: To propel something through air.
examples: He throws the ball to his dog.
She threw the paper into the trash.
He has thrown away old papers.

data.definition: To push or shove forcefully.
examples: He thrusts hands into pockets.
She thrust letter into his hands.
Sword was thrust through target.

data.definition: To journey to a destination.
data.grammar_rule: Requires to before destination.
examples: I travel to France every summer.
data.common_mistake: ❌ Travel in France. ➔ ✅ Travel to France.

data.definition: To crush underfoot or walk on.
examples: Protesters tread on unjust laws.
Marchers trod path through snow.
Grass has been trodden down.

data.pattern: turn down [something] OR turn [something / pronoun] down
data.definition: To reject an offer or invitation, or to reduce the volume/heat.
data.grammar_rule: Separable phrasal verb! Noun objects can go before or after 'down', but pronoun objects MUST go in between (e.g. 'turn IT down').
examples: She turned down the job offer in Paris.
Please turn the music down before midnight.
They offered him a promotion, but he turned it down.
data.common_mistake: ❌ He turned down it. ➔ ✅ He turned it down.

data.pattern: turn off [device / light] OR turn [it] off
data.definition: To stop the operation of an appliance or light switch.
data.grammar_rule: Separable phrasal verb. Pronoun objects MUST go between verb and particle ('turn it off').
examples: Don't forget to turn off the computer before leaving.
He turned the television off.
data.common_mistake: ❌ Turn off it before bedtime. ➔ ✅ Turn it off before bedtime.

data.pattern: turn on [device / light] OR turn [it] on
data.definition: To start the operation of an appliance or light switch.
data.grammar_rule: Separable phrasal verb. Pronoun objects MUST go between verb and particle ('turn it on').
examples: Please turn on the lights when it gets dark.
Could you turn the radio on?
data.common_mistake: ❌ Turn on it please. ➔ ✅ Turn it on please.

data.pattern: turn up (arrive - VI) / turn up [volume/heat] (VT separable)
data.definition: To arrive or appear unexpectedly (VI), or increase volume/sound (VT separable).
data.grammar_rule: Intransitive for arrival ('He turned up late'). Separable transitive for volume ('turn it up').
examples: He turned up at the party without an invitation.
Could you turn up the radio? I love this song.
Turn it up!
data.common_mistake: ❌ Turn up it. ➔ ✅ Turn it up.
